intent: 30 candidates, 24 of them Egyptian — eighty per cent, against a two-thirds target — because the catalogue is 27.6% Egyptian and the goal is past 30%. Weighted hard to substantial everyday food rather than to whatever is easy to keep under five lines: seven one-pot or oven meals built on meat or poultry, four legume and vegetable mains, three soups people actually make for lunch, two fish, two breakfasts, two breads. Nothing already tried is here. The nine twice-refused dishes from batches 1 and 2, the exhausted batch-3 rejects, belila, gibna-bel-tamatem, sogo2-bel-salsa and the held black-bean-soup are all out of the pool and stay in history only. Eleven candidates also exist to use catalogue rows no recipe touches: black-eyed-peas, green-fava-beans, pumpkin, walnuts, herring, pigeon, veal, chicken-drumstick, molasses, green-peas, semit.

candidates.name: Black-Eyed Peas in Tomato and Oil
candidates.note: The cheapest hot lunch in this list and the black-eyed-pea row is used by nothing. One pot, no meat, keeps for days.

candidates.name: Green Fava Beans with Garlic and Coriander
candidates.note: What Egypt eats in spring while the beans are green, and the row exists for exactly this with no recipe on it.

candidates.name: Egyptian Chicken Soup
candidates.note: A real gap: 192 recipes and not one plain chicken soup, which is the thing an Egyptian kitchen makes when somebody is ill.

candidates.name: Potato and Beef Tagine
candidates.note: The clay-pot dinner. Distinct from the stuffed potatoes and from the kofta tagine already in the catalogue: this one is chunks of beef and potato under tomato.

candidates.name: Stuffed Courgettes
candidates.note: Only cabbage mahshi exists. Courgette is the one most households actually make, and the two are not the same dish on a plate.

candidates.name: Grilled Kofta Skewers
candidates.note: Five lines and a grill. The catalogue has baked kofta in a tagine and stewed beef, and nothing off a skewer.

candidates.name: Smoked Herring with Onion and Lemon
candidates.note: Sham el-Nessim on a plate. Five lines, no cooking, and the herring row is used by nothing.

candidates.name: Baked Fish in Tahini Sauce
candidates.note: The other thing Egypt does with bolti besides grilling it. Sayadeya is fish with rice; this is fish under a tahini sauce that splits if you rush it.

candidates.name: Baladi Flatbread
candidates.note: Four lines and the single most-eaten thing in the country. The catalogue bakes pita and focaccia and not this.

candidates.name: Tahini with Black Honey
candidates.note: Two lines, eaten with bread for breakfast across the country, and the black-molasses row is used by almost nothing.

candidates.name: Pumpkin Soup
candidates.note: Winter, cheap, and the pumpkin row has no recipe at all.

candidates.name: Circassian Chicken with Walnuts
candidates.note: Came through the Ottoman kitchens and stayed; it is on Cairo menus as شركسية. Substantial, and the walnut row is unused.

candidates.name: Potatoes and Eggs
candidates.note: Five lines, one pan, and it is what an Egyptian kitchen makes when the fridge is nearly empty. Breakfast is still the thinnest meal type.

candidates.name: Stuffed Pigeon
candidates.note: The dish Egyptians take visitors out for, and the pigeon row has no recipe. Harder photography, worth one attempt.

candidates.name: Oven-Braised Veal Shank
candidates.note: Friday lunch. Long, cheap cut, almost no work, and the veal row is used by nothing.

candidates.name: Oven Chicken Drumsticks
candidates.note: The cheapest chicken there is, one tray. The drumstick row was argued over at length in the ontology work and still has no recipe.

candidates.name: Layered Ghee Pastry
candidates.note: Four lines. The cheese feteer in the catalogue is the stuffed one; this is the plain layered bread it is built from.

candidates.name: Vegetable Soup
candidates.note: Ordinary on purpose: it is the soup that gets made on a weeknight, and nothing in the catalogue answers it.

candidates.name: Sesame Bread Rings
candidates.note: Street bread, five lines, and the semit row is unused. Identity risk on review: Turkish simit is the same shape and a different bread.

candidates.name: One-Pot Chicken and Rice
candidates.note: Chicken cooked on top of the rice so the rice takes the fat. One pot, six lines, feeds a family.

candidates.name: Peas and Beef Stew
candidates.note: One of the four or five stews on rotation in most Egyptian houses, and the green-pea row has no recipe.

candidates.name: Potato Eggah
candidates.note: Five lines. The baladi eggah in the catalogue is the herb one; this is the thick potato one, and they are different meals.

candidates.name: Meatballs in Tomato Sauce
candidates.note: Stovetop, thirty minutes, eaten over rice. Distinct from the baked kofta tagine and from the stewed beef already here.

candidates.name: Festive Rice with Nuts and Raisins
candidates.note: What goes beside the roast at a family lunch. Distinct from the vermicelli rice and the baked ruz moammar already in the catalogue.

candidates.name: Pasta in Minced Beef Sauce
candidates.note: Not an Egyptian dish and completely normal in an Egyptian kitchen. The catalogue has plain tomato macaroni and bechamel and nothing with a meat sauce.

candidates.name: Beef in Cream Sauce
candidates.note: On the menu of nearly every Cairo family restaurant and made at home from cooking cream. Substantial, and nothing in the catalogue uses cream as a sauce.

candidates.name: Baked Potato with Cheese
candidates.note: Five lines and an oven. Made here with roumy, which is the hard cheese an Egyptian fridge actually holds.

candidates.name: Chicken and Sweetcorn Soup
candidates.note: Ordered constantly in Egypt and made at home from a tin. The sweetcorn row is unused.

candidates.name: Potato and Leek Soup
candidates.note: Six lines, one pot, blended or not. The leek row is used by nothing.

candidates.name: Green Beans in Tomato with Beef
candidates.note: Cooked from Beirut to Cairo and the green-bean row has no recipe. A different bean and a different dish from the white-bean stew that found nothing in batch 3.
